sources.title: Renewable Transport Fuel Obligation statistics 2025 fifth provisional release
facts: DfT's fifth provisional 2025 RTFO release uses data available as of 7 July 2026 and remains incomplete until the final report planned for November 2026.
Renewable-fuel volumes, RTFC balances and carbon/sustainability characteristics have transport-fuel scope and are not land-parcel emissions measurements.

sources.title: Prepare for the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism collection
facts: HMRC's collection describes preparation for UK CBAM from 1 January 2027, including record keeping, registration and embodied-emissions guidance.
CBAM applies to specified imported goods and their embodied emissions, not greenhouse-gas emissions from an English land parcel.

sources.title: Keeping records for Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism
facts: HMRC requires importers using actual emissions to retain verification evidence and states default values must be used when verified actual data is unavailable.
Record-keeping requirements and imported-product emissions intensity are not direct parcel measurements.

sources.title: Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism policy summary detailed webpage
facts: The detailed HMRC policy summary distinguishes actual verified emissions intensity from government default emissions values and explains monitoring and verification rules.
CBAM functional units and embodied-emissions calculations have imported-goods scope and must not be converted into parcel emissions.

sources.title: CBAM System Boundaries document version 1.00
facts: The system-boundaries document defines production processes relevant to direct embodied emissions and links installation emissions to production-process attribution.
A production-system boundary for imported goods is not a cadastral or land-parcel boundary.

sources.title: CBAM force of law notice and reference document
facts: HMRC states the draft force-of-law notice has not commenced and is intended to take effect from 1 January 2027.
The page links the system-boundaries reference and carbon-pricing verification form; draft legal status must not be treated as current measured emissions.

sources.title: Check if you will need to register for CBAM collection
facts: HMRC's collection explains CBAM registration liability for importers of in-scope goods from 1 January 2027.
Registration thresholds and liability status are tax-administration evidence, not physical emissions measurements.

sources.title: Work out the date you will need to register for CBAM
facts: HMRC guidance describes when importers must register based on expected or realised value of CBAM goods.
A monetary registration threshold is not an emissions quantity and cannot proxy parcel emissions.

sources.title: RTFO and SAF statistics publication frequency results
facts: DfT published results of engagement on reducing the frequency of provisional RTFO and SAF Mandate statistical releases.
Publication-frequency decisions change release cadence, not the physical emissions represented by fuel data.

sources.title: RTFO and SAF statistics publication frequency detailed results
facts: The detailed DfT response explains changes to the provisional publication schedule and the rationale for fewer releases.
Release scheduling must remain distinct from provisional-versus-final data status and from emissions measurements.

sources.title: UK ETS Cost Containment Mechanism trigger prices and monthly prices full tables
facts: DESNZ publishes CCM trigger prices and monthly average UK allowance market prices, including 2026 monitoring periods.
Allowance market prices and trigger thresholds are market-policy data and not physical greenhouse-gas measurements.

sources.title: UK ETS future markets policy main Authority response accessible webpage
facts: The UK ETS Authority response retains and inflation-proofs the Auction Reserve Price and retains the Cost Containment Mechanism.
Market-stability policy and allowance-price mechanisms are not observed facility or parcel emissions.

sources.title: UK Parliament SI 2026 214 UK ETS Auctioning Amendment Regulations
facts: UK Parliament records SI 2026/214 as laid on 5 March 2026 and in force from 8 April 2026.
The statutory instrument changes auctioning rules and reserve-price treatment; legislation does not itself measure physical emissions.

sources.title: UK Parliament timeline for SI 2026 214
facts: The parliamentary timeline records making, laying, commencement and scrutiny milestones for SI 2026/214.
Legislative timeline events are provenance/currentity evidence, not emissions observations.

sources.title: ONS Energy use bridging table current edition
facts: ONS provides the relationship between Environmental Accounts energy-use measures and DUKES for 1990 to 2024.
A bridging table reconciles accounting frameworks and does not create parcel-level activity or emissions measurements.

sources.title: ONS Atmospheric emissions road transport current edition
facts: ONS publishes emissions generated from fuel sources used by UK road-transport vehicles for 1990 to 2024 and documents revision history.
National road-transport emissions by fuel/pollutant are not emissions measurements for an individual land parcel.

sources.title: ONS Atmospheric emissions bridging tables current edition
facts: ONS bridging tables relate Environmental Accounts atmospheric-emissions measures to UNFCCC and UNECE measures for 1990 to 2024.
Accounting reconciliation must preserve territorial/residence boundaries and cannot be used as parcel attribution.

sources.title: National Data Library Energy Trends and Prices monthly data
facts: The National Data Library catalogues DESNZ monthly energy production, trade, generation, consumption and price releases under the Open Government Licence.
Energy and price statistics are aggregate activity/market data, not parcel greenhouse-gas measurements.

sources.title: Energy Trends UK solid fuels and derived gases
facts: DESNZ publishes coal and coal-related production, trade, consumption and stock statistics, with quarterly and monthly tables.
Solid-fuel activity data requires a supported emissions method before use as emissions and cannot be assigned directly to parcels.

sources.title: Energy trends and prices May to July 2026 announcement
facts: DESNZ schedules the May-to-July 2026 monthly Energy Trends and Prices release for 30 July 2026 at 09:30.
As of 26 July 2026 this is future-release metadata; unreleased statistics are not observed values.

sources.title: Energy trends and prices June to August 2026 announcement
facts: DESNZ schedules the June-to-August 2026 monthly Energy Trends and Prices release for 27 August 2026 at 09:30.
Future production, consumption and price statistics must not be treated as observed before release.

sources.title: Energy Trends April to June 2026 announcement
facts: DESNZ schedules the second-quarter 2026 Energy Trends release for 29 September 2026 at 09:30.
Quarterly future-release metadata is not observed energy activity or emissions evidence.

sources.title: Energy Trends July to September 2026 announcement
facts: DESNZ schedules the third-quarter 2026 Energy Trends release for 17 December 2026 at 09:30.
Unreleased quarterly energy values cannot be used as observed activity or emissions.

sources.title: Energy Trends October to December 2026 announcement
facts: DESNZ lists the fourth-quarter 2026 Energy Trends release for provisional March 2027.
A future publication schedule does not supply observed 2026 energy or emissions values.

sources.title: Draft CBAM Emissions and Verification Regulations consultation
facts: HMRC's technical consultation covers draft requirements for embodied-emissions calculation, monitoring and verification intended for CBAM from 1 January 2027.
Draft consultation requirements are policy/legal design evidence and are not observed parcel emissions.
